Practical therapy for steady change

I guide adults through anxiety, trauma recovery, relationship transitions and burnout with clear, evidence-informed methods and close collaboration.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

Telehealth & in-person in {{CITY}}, {{STATE}} • {{THERAPIST_NAME}}, {{LICENSE}}

Foundational commitments

How I work with people — consistent, clear, and respectful of your context.

  • Confidentiality

    Sessions are private; I maintain clinical records with care and share limits to confidentiality upfront.

  • Collaboration

    We set measurable goals together and track progress. Therapy is an active, joint process.

  • Practicality

    Interventions are selected for real-world impact — skills you can use between sessions.

Approach & Methods

A tailored integration of evidence-based practices.

CBT & Skills

Practical cognitive and behavioral tools to reduce anxiety and manage distressing patterns.

Trauma-Informed Care

Stabilization, pacing, and somatic awareness to safely process distressing experiences.

Systems & Relationships

Focused work on communication, boundaries, and relational patterns that shape well-being.

Modalities: {{MODALITIES}}

Common concerns

  • "Therapy will just drag up the past."

    I prioritize safety and choice — you control pacing and what we address in each session.

  • "I don’t know if it will help me."

    We start with clear goals and review progress regularly; if it's not useful, I’ll help you find alternatives.

  • "I can’t afford long-term therapy."

    I offer focused short-term plans and can discuss referrals to lower-cost community resources.

Client reflections

Feedback shared with permission; anonymized for privacy.

"I learned specific skills that helped me manage panic attacks and set healthier boundaries at work. {{THERAPIST_NAME}} was direct, calm, and practical." — A. (client, anonymized)
"The sessions felt collaborative and grounded. I made steady progress on relationship problems I'd been stuck on for years." — J. (client, anonymized)

Starter Guide: First Steps in Therapy

A concise worksheet: three conversations to have in the first month, practical grounding exercises, and how to evaluate progress.

Ready to begin?

Schedule a 20-minute consultation to see whether we're a fit. I’ll listen, outline early steps, and answer scope or logistics questions.
